acceptance_table.rationale: Locked fixtures.pass[0]: the one off-path command has a stated reason.
Locked fixtures.fail[0]: an off-path cron command listed with no reason; deterministic_check fails for a listed off-path command without a reason, a stated state that breaks the rule.

Owner item 5: name which go through; reasons only 'for any that do not'. The item closes the off-path set as empty, so every off-path command (none) has a reason; deterministic_check holds. Penalising full routing would invert the owner's goal ('Cron commands use the shared command path').
Mixed set: the single off-path command has a stated reason.
Known-bad: cron.list is stated to be off the path and no reason appears anywhere; deterministic_check fails for a listed off-path command.
Two off-path commands, only cron.end has a reason; cron.list has none, so 'a reason for each' is unmet and the check fails.
The anchor's allowed exception: an off-path command is acceptable when its reason is stated.
Explicitly rejects the reason obligation for off-path commands.
In scope (changes a cron command) but says nothing about which cron commands are on or off the shared path or why; silence is omission, not conflict.
Mentions the topic but neither identifies which cron commands are off the path nor gives reasons nor states that none is off.
Outside scope: no cron command, sc-cron-commands or shared command path change.
